title: fail to deploy functions that use deno workspace packages
body:
# Bug report

- [X] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application. 
- [X] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). 

## Describe the bug

functions deploy fails to deploy functions with workspace dependencies

## To Reproduce

See the following project: https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/elastic-chatterjee-forked-6496py?workspaceId=ws_VGZMLHNu2hWPYZLrXEYbsU

you can see the supabase function in supabase/functions/example. Attempting to deploy this will fail. However `deno run index.ts` works as expected

## Expected behavior

`pnpx supabase functions deploy` deploys the function and resolves the workspace dependencies in the same way that deno does.

## Screenshots

If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

## System information

- Version of supabase-js: 2.20.12
- Version of Node.js: v22.14.0

## Additional context

note that it fails with the following error:
```
Relative import path "@wovenlibs/core" not prefixed with / or ./ or ../ and not in import map
```

because deno can resolve the workspace packages without a scheme. But it seems supabase cannot resolve workspace files in the same way.

comments.author: kallebysantos
comments.body:
Hey @nyannyacha 💚 
> ... recently merged https://github.com/supabase/cli/pull/3417 seems related to this

Not really 😔 My PR only covers the module graph for local development and requires that `imports` need to be declared inside `supabase/functions/[slug]/deno.json(c)` or in the file defined at `config.toml`. 

@alita-moore after looking your example, I could see that you have the following `import_map` config:

<details>
<summary>config.toml</summary>

```toml
[functions.example]
enabled = true
verify_jwt = true
import_map = "./functions/example/deno.json"
```

</details>

I'm not sure about `Deno's workspaces` neither `@scope/` but based on my understanding the CLI will try to use this `import_map` to resolve your function deps. Also outside imports feat may requires the `--use-api` while deploying like [described here](https://github.com/orgs/supabase/discussions/33613)

---

<details>
<summary>Possible fix:</summary>

Apply the following config to your `supabase/functions/[slug]/deno.json(c)`
```json
{
    "imports":  {
        "@scope/": "../../../libs/"
    }
}
```
> For large project with many functions, you can also define a global `import_map.json` then point it inside your `config.toml`. In a future release you'll be also able to define `importMap` field directly from your `supabase/functions/[slug]/deno.json(c)`

Local development:
```
npx supabase@beta functions serve
```

Then deploy with:
```
npx supabase functions deploy --use-api 
```

I hope that it helps 💚

</details>

comments.author: nyannyacha
comments.body:
> If I implement the fix you suggested with --use-api I get the following

In this case, the backend that performs bundling is on the Supabase side and does not yet support Deno 2, so this is expected behavior.

cc @laktek 

> it appears to resolve the dependency when building it, but then the resulting function gives the following error at boot

As mentioned above, Supabase Edge Functions does not yet support Deno 2. This is expected behavior because function bundles made in the latest version of the edge runtime (v1.68.0-develop.13, Deno 2) cannot yet be loaded by the service.

I am able to resolve this by setting up a `deno.json` script that points to the .js artifact in each of the package's roots. e.g.
```
{
  "name": "@wovendomain/core",
  "exports": {
    ".": "./dist/src/index.js"
  },
}
```

but this is not ideal because it causes deno to lose its inferred types (because it points only to the .js file) and because these packages are not deno, so it adds confusion.

comments.author: nyannyacha
comments.body:
> and then add the package to a package.json

> it would be nice if I could also get rid of the package.json as it seems unnecessary in this case. 

There is no need to have package.json under `supabase/functions/example`.

Simply adding dependencies to the root package.json as shown below was sufficient:
```diff
  "name": "workspace",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "",
  "main": "index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1"
  },
  "keywords": [],
  "author": "",
  "license": "ISC",
  "packageManager": "pnpm@10.8.1",
+ "dependencies": {
+   "@scope/lib": "workspace:*"
+ }
```

Then running `deno install` or `pnpm install` to update the node_modules folder and make a bundle and it worked fine too (both deno compile and edge runtime).

comments.author: alita-moore
comments.body:
generally speaking, it's not great to place packages in the root package.json because then you're requiring all other packages to rely on the same dependency. In my local setup it seems that deno resolves the dependency even without defining it in the `package.json` at all. For example, in [this](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/elastic-chatterjee-forked-2tz9hf?workspaceId=ws_VGZMLHNu2hWPYZLrXEYbsU) codesandbox, I remove the `package.json` from supabase/functions/example and do not add the package to the root `package.json` and it successfully compiles. Notably, this works in both deno version `2.2.10` and `2.1.4` (the current deno version in the edge runtime). From what I can tell the edge runtime serve the functions with this setup as well. To be honest, I'm now struggling to reproduce the issue where it would claim the imports were invalid relative paths, now if I deploy using deno version 2 along with the workaround I mentioned earlier where I include the [relevant source files in the import map](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/35021#issuecomment-2807906173) along with the workaround for the package entrypoint resolution mentioned [here](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/35021#issuecomment-2808449435) it seems to deploy and serve properly.

That's all to say that I think there are the folllowing issues for getting this workflow up and running:
1. support deno 2 on the edge runtime service
2. automatically detect workspace files and include them during the deployment to avoid [this](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/35021#issuecomment-2807906173) hack
3. upgrade the edge runtime to a deno version after they fix this issue: https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/28926

comments.author: kallebysantos

Hi @lilnamcor 💚

> Why is the behavior not consistent is my main concern

Based on my understanding the standard approach uses docker do bundle your assets in the same way of local development bundling, with a little difference that now local `serve` is also resolving the module graph PR https://github.com/supabase/cli/pull/3417  - uses the same way as `--use-api` .

The new way is by using the `--use-api`, it will apply a recursive module graph introspection to resolve your local files.

> isn't working whereas before it sometimes worked

May you check your supabase cli version? as well if your imports is well defined, since there's a lot of `../` it may can be a wrong path. Also, is your project working locally with `functions serve`?
